source_text: Ὅτι γὰρ ἔμπροσθεν ἐγένετο παρὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων, μαρτυροῦσιν αἱ πανταχοῦ τῆς οἰκουμένης Ἐκκλησίαι, καὶ δῆμοι, καὶ πόλεις, καὶ ἔθνη προσδραμόντα τοῖς ἰδιώταις καὶ ἁλιεῦσιν. Οὐ γὰρ ἂν τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐκράτησαν οἱ ἀγράμματοι καὶ πτωχοὶ καὶ πένητες καὶ εὐτελεῖς, εἰ μὴ τὴν τῶν σημείων εἶχον βοήθειαν. Πλὴν ἀλλ' οὔτε σὺ τῆς τοῦ Πνεύματος ἔρημος γέγονας χάριτος, ἀλλὰ πολλὰ ἔτι καὶ νῦν μένει τῆς δωρεᾶς ἐκείνης σύμβολα, αὐτῶν τούτων τῶν ἀπηριθμημένων πολλῷ μείζονα καὶ θαυμαστότερα· οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἴσον σῶμα τελευτῆσαν ἀναστῆσαι, καὶ ψυχὴν νεκρωθεῖσαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἀπαλλάξαι τῆς ἀπωλείας ἐκείνης, ὃ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος γίνεται· οὐκ ἔστιν ἴσον νοσήματα ἀπελάσαι σαρκὸς, καὶ ἁμαρτιῶν φορτίον ἀποθέσθαι· οὐκ ἔστιν ἴσον ὄμμα πεπηρωμένον διορθῶσαι, καὶ ψυχὴν ἐσκοτισμένην φωτὶ καταλάμψαι. Εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἦν ἀῤῥαβὼν τοῦ Πνεύματος καὶ νῦν, οὐκ ἂν συνέστη τὸ βάπτισμα, οὐκ ἂν ἁμαρτημάτων ἄφεσις ἐγένετο. οὐκ ἂν δικαιοσύνη καὶ ἁγιασμὸς, οὐκ ἂν υἱοθεσίαν ἐλάβομεν, οὐκ ἂν μυστηρίων ἀπελαύσαμεν· σῶμα γὰρ καὶ αἷμα μυστικὸν οὐκ ἄν ποτε γένοιτο τῆς τοῦ Πνεύματος χάριτος χωρίς· οὐκ ἂν ἱερέας ἐσχήκαμεν· οὐδὲ γὰρ ταύτας δυνατὸν τὰς χειροτονίας ἄνευ ἐκείνης τῆς ἐπιφοιτήσεως γίνεσθαι. Καὶ ἄλλα δὲ πολλὰ ἔχοι τις ἂν εἰπεῖν τῆς τοῦ Πνεύματος χάριτος σύμβολα. Ὥστε καὶ σὺ τὸν ἀῤῥαβῶνα τοῦ Πνεύματος ἔχεις, καὶ νέκρωσιν ἀπέθου ψυχῆς, καὶ πήρωσιν λογισμῶν, καὶ τὸν ἀκάθαρτον ἀπεδύσω βίον. Μὴ τοίνυν ἀσχάλλωμεν περὶ τῶν μελλόντων, τοιαῦτα λαβόντες ἐνέχυρα· ἀλλὰ πανταχόθεν τὸν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως συλλέξαντες λόγον, καὶ βίον ἄξιον τῶν δογμάτων ἐπιδειξώμεθα τούτων, ἵνα καὶ τῶν ἀκινήτων ἀγαθῶν ἐπιτύχωμεν, τῶν πάντα λόγον ὑπερβαινόντων καὶ νοῦν ἀνθρώπινον· ὧν γένοιτο πάντας ἡμᾶς ἐπιτυχεῖν, χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι' οὗ καὶ μεθ' οὗ ἡ δόξα τῷ Πατρὶ, ἅμα τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The Spirit's present gifts as guarantee of the resurrection
orientation: Chrysostom is answering an objector who says the apostolic signs no longer happen, by arguing that the Spirit's gifts still remain in the Church as a guarantee of the resurrection.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'guarantee' for ἀρραβών, and the genitive Πνεύματος is rendered as 'of the Spirit' to preserve the source's possessive force.
The source uses σύμβολα for the remaining signs of the Spirit's gift; 'symbols' preserves the sense of visible tokens or marks.
ἐνέχυρα means securities or pledges given as assurance; 'pledges' keeps the commercial metaphor of a guarantee for future goods.

choices.term: ἀγράμματοι καὶ πτωχοὶ καὶ πένητες καὶ εὐτελεῖς
choices.english: unlettered and poor and needy and lowly men
choices.why: The four adjectives describe the apostles' low social status; each is rendered distinctly to preserve the rhetorical accumulation.
rejected: illiterate and poor and destitute and worthless men

choices.why: ἀκίνητος means unmoved, unshakable; 'immovable' preserves the sense of goods that cannot be shaken or taken away.

pass_b_english: That these things happened before through the apostles is witnessed by the churches everywhere in the world, and by peoples, cities, and nations who ran to laymen and fishermen. For unlettered and poor and needy and lowly men would never have prevailed over the world if they had not had the help of signs. But neither have you been left without the grace of the Spirit. Even now many symbols of that gift remain, far greater and more wonderful than the ones just listed. For it is not the same thing to raise a body that has died and to deliver a soul that has been killed by sins from that destruction—which happens through baptism. It is not the same thing to drive out diseases of the flesh and to put off the burden of sins. It is not the same thing to restore a blinded eye and to illuminate a darkened soul with light. For if there were not a guarantee of the Spirit even now, baptism would not have been established, forgiveness of sins would not have come to be, righteousness and holiness would not have come, we would not have received adoption as sons, we would not have enjoyed the mysteries. For the mystical body and blood could never have come to be without the grace of the Spirit. We would not have had priests, for these ordinations cannot happen without that visitation. And one could name many other symbols of the grace of the Spirit. So you too have the guarantee of the Spirit, and you have put off the death of the soul, the maiming of your thoughts, and you have stripped off the unclean life. Let us not be distressed about the things to come, since we have received such pledges. Instead, let us gather from every side the argument for the resurrection, and let us show a life worthy of these doctrines, so that we may also obtain the immovable good things that surpass every word and human mind. May we all obtain them, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom and with whom be glory to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, to the ages of ages. Amen.

problems.why: ἰδιῶται means 'laymen/commoners', not 'unskilled men'; these were ordinary people, not necessarily lacking skill.
problems.ruling: ἰδιῶται means laymen/commoners, not 'unskilled men'; mistranslates the word's core sense.

problems.why: πήρωσις means 'maiming/mutilation', not 'blinding'; λογισμοί are 'thoughts/reasonings', not 'reasoning' as a faculty.
problems.ruling: πήρωσις means maming/mutilation, not 'blinding'; eye imagery in context makes error misleading.

fixed: Changed 'unskilled men' to 'laymen' for ἰδιώταις, which means commoners/laymen rather than unskilled.
Changed 'the blinding of your reasoning' to 'the maiming of your thoughts' for πήρωσιν λογισμῶν, since πήρωσις is maiming/mutilation and λογισμοί are thoughts.

last_rejected.why: ἰδιώταις means 'uneducated/ordinary men', not specifically 'laymen' (non-clergy); the contrast is social/intellectual, not clerical.
last_rejected.ruling: ἰδιῶταις can mean 'private/ordinary men' vs. apostles; 'laymen' fits the ordinary-vs-apostle contrast adequately.

last_rejected.why: νέκρωσις means 'deadening/mortification', not 'death'; it's the process of being made dead, parallel to 'maiming' and 'stripping off'.
last_rejected.ruling: νέκρωσις as 'death' is within normal range; 'deadening' is preferable but not a meaning-changing error.

last_rejected.why: πήρωσις means 'blindness/maiming' but λογισμοί are 'reasonings/reckonings', not 'thoughts' in general; better 'blindness of reasonings' or 'maimed reasonings'.
last_rejected.ruling: λογισμῶν as 'thoughts' is within normal range; 'reasonings' is a preference, not a major error.
